BACE simulation study: does it recover the truth under missing data?

Published

August 8, 2026

What changed since the 2026-07 report

The 2026-07 run of this study surfaced poor interval coverage (gaussian ~0.76, poisson ~0.69), catastrophic poisson imputations, and near-chance categorical recovery. A four-way root-cause investigation (2026-08, adversarially verified; full write-up in .agents/investigation-2026-08.md) found six defects and fixed them:

  1. Improper final-phase MI (the dominant bug): bace_final_imp fit every final model on the convergence chain’s point imputations as if observed — response NAs are now reinstated so MCMCglmm does data augmentation.
  2. Finite-draw metric ceiling: the 95% PI formed from the empirical 2.5–97.5% quantiles of n_final draws covers at most 0.95\,(m-1)/(m+1) (~0.845 at m=15) even for a perfect imputer; this report now also reports a ceiling-free t-interval (cover95_t) and probability-based discrete prediction sets (cover95_prob).
  3. Poisson point estimate was a mean of lognormals (one chain excursion ⇒ million-count imputations, frozen everywhere by defect 1) — now a median-based rate with a data-adaptive guard (3·max observed + 5).
  4. Priors: gaussian R back to Hadfield’s (V=1, ν=0.002) — the 2026-04 ν=2 setting inflated residual variance ~3× and biased λ̂ down; poisson gets log-link-scaled priors (R: V=0.1, ν=1; PX working prior α.V=1).
  5. Degenerate categorical DGP: all K−1 liabilities shared one linear predictor (Bayes balanced-accuracy ceiling ≈ 0.50 — the old 0.43–0.46 was near-optimal, not a failure). The DGP now draws distinct per-liability slopes and random effects, and the per-replicate Bayes ceiling is reported alongside BACE’s accuracy. The categorical default also switched to the true multinomial model (ovr_categorical = FALSE).
  6. Type detection: integer variables were assigned poisson vs gaussian by a marginal AIC race that misfired exactly under strong phylogenetic signal — now deterministic (non-negative integers ⇒ poisson).

Pre-fix outputs are archived in archive_2026-07_prebugfix/ and compared against below (Section 5.3).

1 Aims

Evaluate whether BACE recovers the truth when data are missing: are its imputed values and the parameters estimated from them unbiased, are its uncertainty intervals calibrated, and does this hold across response distributions and missingness mechanisms?

2 What simulations we did

Two studies, both on sim_bace() with production MCMC (nitt 4–5k, burnin 0.8–1k, thin 4–5, n_final 15–20).

Study Response Mechanisms Replicates Purpose
A gaussian, known slope MCAR, MAR 40 each parameter recovery: slope bias + CI coverage, vs an oracle and complete-case
B gaussian, poisson, binary, ordinal, categorical MCAR, MAR 1000 each value recovery, bias, and interval calibration for every response type

Study B is 5 types × 2 mechanisms × 1000 reps = 10,000 datasets (9997 completed).

3 Settings, model structure, and provenance

Simulated model structure.

  • Study A (dev/12_recovery_simulation.R): pure-birth tree (ape::rtree, Grafen branch lengths, depth-normalised to 1); phylogenetically correlated predictor x \sim \mathrm{MVN}(0, R) and phylogenetic effect u \sim \mathrm{MVN}(0, R) on the tree correlation matrix R; response y = b_0 + b_1 x + u + \varepsilon, \varepsilon \sim N(0, \sigma_e^2) (true values in the table below). Missingness on y only: MCAR at a constant rate; MAR with \Pr(\text{missing}) = \mathrm{plogis}\{a + \text{mar\_slope}\cdot z(x)\} — depends on the observed predictor. Analysis pipeline per replicate: bace_imp() → assess_convergence() → bace_final_imp() → with_imputations(gls) → pool_mi(), against oracle (full data) and complete-case comparators.
  • Study B (dev/13_response_type_simulation.R, v3): data from sim_bace() — one response (gaussian / poisson / binary / threshold3 ordinal / multinomial3 categorical) plus two gaussian predictors, all three variables with the phylogenetic-signal proportion below; known predictor effects \beta_{x_1}, \beta_{x_2} (below); one row per species. Discrete responses are generated on the latent liability scale (the multinomial DGP draws distinct per-liability slopes and random effects and records the per-replicate Bayes ceiling). Missingness on the response only, same MCAR/MAR mechanisms as Study A (MAR depends on observed x_1).

4 Measures (what they mean)

For each replicate we hide 30% of the response, impute with BACE, and compare to the known truth; averages over replicates carry Monte Carlo standard errors (MCSE).

  • Bias (standardised): \big(\overline{\hat y} - \overline{y}\big)/\mathrm{SD}(y) on hidden cells (0 = unbiased); categorical uses total-variation distance of class proportions.
  • Coverage — two estimators per family:
    • cover95 (quantile; kept for comparability with 2026-07): truth inside the empirical 2.5–97.5% range of the n_final draws. Ceiling ≈ 0.831 at 15 draws even for a perfect imputer — read it against that ceiling, not against 0.95.
    • cover95_t (continuous): \bar y_{draws} \pm t_{m-1,.975}\, s_{draws}\sqrt{1+1/m} — no finite-draw ceiling; target 0.95. cover95_prob (discrete): smallest class set reaching 0.95 cumulative probability under the models’ averaged class-probability matrices; target ≥ 0.95.
  • Recovery: correlation (continuous; plus Spearman and log1p-scale for poisson, since Pearson on raw counts is tail-dominated) or balanced accuracy (discrete). Categorical is judged against its per-replicate Bayes ceiling (bayes_bal_acc, computed from the true simulated class probabilities).

5 Results

5.1 Study A — parameter recovery (gaussian slope, 40 reps)

Grey band = correct-calibration range at 40 reps. Under MAR, complete-case analysis is a biased sample of the response; BACE removes that bias and its 95% CI covers the true slope at the nominal rate.

Method Mech Slope bias Coverage Mean bias
BACE MAR 0.065 0.950 0.011
complete-case MAR 0.098 0.950 -0.259
oracle MAR 0.071 0.950 0.000
BACE MCAR 0.070 0.975 -0.003
complete-case MCAR 0.045 0.975 -0.002
oracle MCAR 0.057 1.000 0.000

Dotted line = chance (1/3). Star = the categorical Bayes-classifier ceiling given the DGP — balanced accuracy cannot exceed it.

Cover (q) is the 2026-07-comparable quantile estimator — its perfect-imputer ceiling at 15 draws is ≈ 0.83, so values near that ceiling indicate correct calibration.

5.3 Before vs after the 2026-08 fixes


Poisson catastrophe rate P(|std bias| > 1): pre MCAR 0.088 / MAR 0.146  ->  post MCAR 0.028 / MAR 0.065

Note the categorical rows are not a like-for-like comparison: the 2026-08 DGP is non-degenerate (per-liability slopes; Bayes ceiling reported above), whereas the 2026-07 DGP capped balanced accuracy at ~0.50 by construction.
